headline: High: unstructured can read/write files and spawn subprocesses while dbt-core can touch warehouse data, creating default-path leakage and cascading-error risks; prompt injection is lower due to no shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not default. However, unstructured can read_filesystem and write_filesystem, and dbt-core can consume warehouse-related inputs; if outputs are manually copied or placed in a shared file, prompt-like content could influence downstream processing. This is lower than medium because the bridge is not shown in either profile.
conditions: IF both agents are connected through a shared file or clipboard bridge
IF unstructured output is manually fed into dbt-core as trusted text
mitigations: Add a review step before dbt-core consumes any generated text

B_data_leakage.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, and unstructured reads and writes documents locally while also having allowlisted network egress. A shared workspace or file handoff could expose warehouse-derived content to document processing and onward network transmission. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default workflows, but the profiles do not show uncontrolled third-party exfiltration.
conditions: IF warehouse exports are written into files that unstructured reads
IF those files contain sensitive warehouse data
mitigations: Redact sensitive columns before file handoff
Audit outbound destinations for allowlisted egress

C_capability_conflict.rationale: unstructured has write_filesystem, read_filesystem, spawn_subprocesses, and supports multiple instances, while dbt-core can call warehouse APIs and has allowlisted egress. If both operate on the same mutable project or artifact directory, they can overwrite each other's outputs or race on shared state. The profiles do not prove a lock, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact path
IF dbt-core and unstructured run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Run one agent at a time
Add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: dbt-core can produce warehouse-facing transformations, and unstructured can generate extracted text from documents. If dbt-core consumes unstructured output without verification, extraction errors can cascade into incorrect models or warehouse actions. The pair is not documented as an automated chain, so this is medium rather than high, but the pathway is credible.
conditions: IF dbt-core ingests unstructured extraction output as authoritative input
IF no validation step checks extracted fields before transformation
mitigations: Require human review for extracted fields
Compare extracted values against source documents

E_compliance.rationale: dbt-core touches data warehouse data, while unstructured processes documents, images, and text and exposes a privacy-policy endpoint. If regulated warehouse data is exported into document-processing workflows, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific certification mismatch, so this is a compliance-risk medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated warehouse data is exported into unstructured inputs
IF retention or residency rules differ between the warehouse and document-processing workflow
mitigations: Block regulated data from document-processing paths
